01-01.title: Frankenstein
01-01.fact: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein was published anonymously in London on New Year's Day 1818 — the book that invented modern horror.

01-19.title: Edgar Allan Poe
01-19.fact: Edgar Allan Poe, master of the macabre, was born in Boston in 1809.

01-25.title: The Blair Witch Project
01-25.fact: The Blair Witch Project premiered at a midnight Sundance screening in 1999, igniting the found-footage boom.

01-29.title: The Raven
01-29.fact: Poe's 'The Raven' first appeared in print in 1845 and made its author famous almost overnight.

02-01.title: Mary Shelley
02-01.fact: Mary Shelley, who dreamed up Frankenstein at age 18, died on this day in 1851.

02-02.title: Boris Karloff
02-02.fact: Boris Karloff, the screen's definitive Frankenstein monster, died on this day in 1969.

02-05.title: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
02-05.fact: Cold War paranoia classic Invasion of the Body Snatchers first crept into theaters in 1956.
02-05.wiki: Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1956 film)

02-14.title: Dracula
02-14.fact: Universal released Dracula on Valentine's Day 1931 as 'the strangest love story of all' — and 60 years later to the day, The Silence of the Lambs opened in 1991.

02-24.title: Get Out
02-24.fact: Jordan Peele's Get Out opened in 2017, redefining social horror and winning Peele an Oscar for the screenplay.

02-29.title: The Salem Witch Trials
02-29.fact: On leap day 1692, arrest warrants were issued for the first three women accused of witchcraft in Salem.

03-01.title: The Salem Witch Trials
03-01.fact: The first Salem witch examinations began on this day in 1692, when Tituba's confession set off a deadly panic.

03-02.title: King Kong
03-02.fact: King Kong premiered at Radio City Music Hall in 1933, terrifying audiences with the eighth wonder of the world.

03-04.title: Nosferatu
03-04.fact: F.W. Murnau's Nosferatu premiered in Berlin in 1922. A court later ordered every print destroyed as a Dracula rip-off — one survived.

03-13.title: It Follows
03-13.fact: It Follows opened in 2015, turning a slow walk into one of the decade's most dreaded images.

03-15.title: H.P. Lovecraft
03-15.fact: H.P. Lovecraft died poor and obscure in Providence in 1937, decades before his cosmic horror conquered pop culture.

03-22.title: Us
03-22.fact: Jordan Peele's doppelgänger nightmare Us opened in 2019 to one of the biggest original-horror debuts ever.

03-28.title: The Birds
03-28.fact: Alfred Hitchcock's The Birds premiered in New York in 1963 — nature's revenge, with no musical score at all.

03-30.title: The Silence of the Lambs
03-30.fact: On Oscar night 1992, The Silence of the Lambs swept the 'Big Five' awards — still the only horror film to win Best Picture.

04-01.title: Lon Chaney
04-01.fact: Lon Chaney, the 'Man of a Thousand Faces' behind the Phantom of the Opera, was born in 1883.

04-06.title: A Quiet Place
04-06.fact: A Quiet Place opened in 2018 and made entire theaters afraid to eat their popcorn.

04-20.title: Bram Stoker
04-20.fact: Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, died in London in 1912 — the same week the Titanic sank.

04-29.title: Alfred Hitchcock
04-29.fact: Alfred Hitchcock, the Master of Suspense, died on this day in 1980.

05-09.title: Friday the 13th
05-09.fact: Friday the 13th opened in 1980, sending a generation of campers home from Crystal Lake early.

05-23.title: The Shining
05-23.fact: Stanley Kubrick's The Shining opened in 1980. Stephen King famously hated it; audiences never forgot it.

05-25.title: Alien
05-25.fact: Alien opened in American theaters in 1979: in space, no one can hear you scream.

05-26.title: Dracula
05-26.fact: Bram Stoker's Dracula went on sale in London in 1897. Horror legend Peter Cushing was born on the same date in 1913.

05-27.title: Vincent Price & Christopher Lee
05-27.fact: Horror royalty shares this birthday: Vincent Price (1911) and Christopher Lee (1922) were born exactly eleven years apart.

06-04.title: Poltergeist
06-04.fact: Poltergeist opened in 1982 and made an entire generation distrust television static and clown dolls.

06-06.title: The Omen
06-06.fact: The Omen opened on 6/6/76 — a marketing masterstroke for a film about the birth of the Antichrist.

06-07.title: Christopher Lee
06-07.fact: Sir Christopher Lee, Hammer's Dracula across a half-century of screen villainy, died on this day in 2015.

06-08.title: Hereditary
06-08.fact: Ari Aster's Hereditary opened in 2018, giving A24 its biggest hit to date and audiences a new fear of clucking sounds.

06-12.title: Rosemary's Baby
06-12.fact: Rosemary's Baby opened in 1968, bringing the Devil into a Manhattan apartment building.

06-16.title: Psycho
06-16.fact: Psycho premiered in New York in 1960. Hitchcock barred theaters from admitting anyone after it began.

06-20.title: Jaws
06-20.fact: Jaws opened in 1975, inventing the summer blockbuster and emptying beaches across America.

06-25.title: The Thing
06-25.fact: John Carpenter's The Thing opened in 1982 — savaged by critics, ignored by audiences, and later canonized as a masterpiece.

06-26.title: The Lottery
06-26.fact: Shirley Jackson's 'The Lottery' ran in The New Yorker in 1948 and drew the most hate mail in the magazine's history.

07-03.title: Midsommar
07-03.fact: Midsommar opened in 2019, proving horror can be just as terrifying in broad daylight.

07-14.title: The Blair Witch Project
07-14.fact: The Blair Witch Project hit theaters in 1999 — made for around $60,000, it grossed nearly $250 million.

07-16.title: George A. Romero
07-16.fact: George A. Romero, father of the modern zombie film, died on this day in 2017.

07-19.title: The Conjuring
07-19.fact: The Conjuring opened in 2013, launching horror's biggest cinematic universe from a Rhode Island farmhouse.

08-06.title: The Sixth Sense
08-06.fact: The Sixth Sense opened in 1999. Audiences kept its ending secret all summer.

08-08.title: Shirley Jackson
08-08.fact: Shirley Jackson, author of The Haunting of Hill House, died on this day in 1965.

08-11.title: Peter Cushing
08-11.fact: Peter Cushing, Hammer Films' gentleman Van Helsing and Baron Frankenstein, died on this day in 1994.

08-13.title: Alfred Hitchcock
08-13.fact: Alfred Hitchcock, the Master of Suspense, was born in London in 1899.

08-16.title: Bela Lugosi
08-16.fact: Bela Lugosi died on this day in 1956 and was buried wearing his Dracula cape.

08-20.title: H.P. Lovecraft
08-20.fact: H.P. Lovecraft, architect of cosmic horror and the Cthulhu Mythos, was born in Providence in 1890.

08-26.title: Lon Chaney & Tobe Hooper
08-26.fact: A dark double anniversary: silent horror icon Lon Chaney (1930) and Texas Chain Saw Massacre director Tobe Hooper (2017) both died on this day.

08-30.title: Wes Craven
08-30.fact: Wes Craven, creator of Freddy Krueger and Scream, died in 2015 — on the birthday of Frankenstein author Mary Shelley (1797).

09-08.title: It
09-08.fact: It opened in 2017 and floated past every record to become the highest-grossing horror film of all time.

09-21.title: Stephen King
09-21.fact: Stephen King, the modern master of horror, was born in Portland, Maine in 1947.

09-25.title: Paranormal Activity
09-25.fact: Paranormal Activity opened in 2009 — a $15,000 movie that became one of the most profitable films ever made.

10-01.title: Night of the Living Dead
10-01.fact: Night of the Living Dead premiered in Pittsburgh in 1968, and the modern zombie was born.

10-07.title: Edgar Allan Poe
10-07.fact: Edgar Allan Poe died mysteriously in Baltimore in 1849, found delirious in clothes that were not his own.

10-18.title: The Ring
10-18.fact: The Ring opened in 2002, kicking off Hollywood's J-horror wave. Seven days...

10-20.title: Bela Lugosi
10-20.fact: Bela Lugosi, the screen's original Count Dracula, was born in Lugos, Hungary in 1882.

10-25.title: Halloween
10-25.fact: John Carpenter's Halloween premiered in Kansas City in 1978. Fifteen years later to the day, Vincent Price passed away in 1993.

10-29.title: Saw
10-29.fact: Saw opened in 2004, launching the biggest horror franchise of its decade. Do you want to play a game?

10-30.title: The War of the Worlds Broadcast
10-30.fact: On the night before Halloween 1938, Orson Welles's War of the Worlds radio broadcast convinced some listeners that Martians had landed.
10-30.wiki: The War of the Worlds (1938 radio drama)

10-31.title: Harry Houdini
10-31.fact: Harry Houdini died on Halloween 1926. Séances attempting to contact him are still held every October 31.

11-03.title: Godzilla
11-03.fact: Godzilla first rose from the sea in Japanese theaters in 1954, nuclear dread made flesh.

11-08.title: Bram Stoker
11-08.fact: Bram Stoker, the Dublin theater manager who wrote Dracula, was born in 1847.

11-09.title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
11-09.fact: A Nightmare on Elm Street opened in 1984, and Freddy Krueger began haunting America's dreams.

11-13.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
11-13.fact: Francis Ford Coppola's Bram Stoker's Dracula opened in 1992 with a record-setting bite at the box office.

11-16.title: Ed Gein Arrested
11-16.fact: Ed Gein was arrested in Plainfield, Wisconsin in 1957. His crimes inspired Psycho, The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, and The Silence of the Lambs.

11-21.title: Frankenstein
11-21.fact: Universal's Frankenstein opened in 1931. Theaters kept nurses on hand for fainting patrons — 'It's alive!'

11-23.title: Boris Karloff
11-23.fact: Boris Karloff, born William Henry Pratt in London in 1887, became horror's gentlest monster.

12-12.title: The Wolf Man
12-12.fact: The Wolf Man premiered in 1941, giving cinema its definitive werewolf legend — even a man who is pure in heart...

12-14.title: Shirley Jackson
12-14.fact: Shirley Jackson, whose Hill House still isn't sane, was born in 1916.

12-20.title: Scream
12-20.fact: Wes Craven's Scream opened in 1996, resurrecting the slasher by teaching it the rules.

12-26.title: The Exorcist
12-26.fact: The Exorcist opened the day after Christmas 1973 — lines around the block, fainting audiences, and waiting ambulances.
